title: AI-Assisted Software Development: Team Profiles and Capabilities for Putting Research into Action
gist: Nathen Harvey, presenting DORA's 2025 State of AI-Assisted Software Development research at QCon London, argues AI is an amplifier whose returns depend on the underlying organizational system rather than the tooling. The headline finding is a contradiction: as AI adoption rose, perceived individual effectiveness and code quality both improved while software delivery instability also increased, pointing to misaligned incentives and missing visibility into production impact.

themes.theme: AI as Amplifier of the Organizational System

insights.claim: AI's primary role in software development is as an amplifier, so the greatest returns come from a strategic focus on the underlying organizational system rather than on the tools themselves.
insights.speaker: Ben Linders
insights.so_what: Implies AI coding-tool ROI is conditional on organizational maturity, which caps the value a vendor can deliver to a dysfunctional buyer and explains uneven enterprise results.
insights.quote: The greatest returns on your investments in AI are going to come from a strategic focus on the underlying organizational system.
insights.locator: AI's primary role in software development is that of an amplifier

insights.claim: Without an organizational foundation, AI tends to create localized pockets of productivity that are subsequently lost to downstream chaos.
insights.speaker: Ben Linders
insights.so_what: Local productivity metrics from AI pilots are systematically misleading as a basis for scaling spend - measure end-to-end delivery, not developer-level speed.
insights.quote: Without that foundation, AI tends to create localized pockets of productivity that are often lost to downstream chaos.
insights.locator: AI's primary role in software development is that of an amplifier

insights.claim: As AI adoption increased, self-reported individual effectiveness saw the highest increase relative to every other aspect DORA examined, and perceptions of code quality also improved.
insights.speaker: Ben Linders
insights.so_what: Perceived effectiveness is the strongest AI signal in the data, which is exactly why self-reported productivity gains are a weak basis for valuing AI dev-tool vendors.
insights.locator: As AI adoption increased, the perceived impact

insights.claim: Software delivery instability increased alongside improved perceived code quality, meaning teams are more likely to see deployments rolled back or hot fixes required to correct errors introduced by new deployments.
insights.speaker: Ben Linders
insights.so_what: AI adoption is empirically raising production defect rates even as developers feel better about quality - a direct tailwind for testing, rollback and incident-response tooling.
insights.locator: Interestingly, while individual effectiveness and code quality improved

insights.claim: The contradiction between rising perceived code quality and rising delivery instability may signal misaligned incentives or a lack of visibility into the impact of changes, as happens when an engineer is measured on shipping features rather than on how those features land in production.
insights.speaker: Ben Linders
insights.so_what: Points the fix at incentive design and production feedback loops rather than at model quality - relevant to which layer of the AI dev stack captures budget next.
insights.locator: This contradiction- increased code quality and software delivery instability

themes.theme: Seven Team Profiles as a Diagnostic Framework

insights.claim: DORA identified seven distinct team profiles in its data - foundational challenges, the legacy bottleneck, constrained by process, high impact low cadence, stable and methodical, pragmatic performers, and harmonious high-achievers - measured across team performance, product performance, effectiveness, friction and burnout.
insights.speaker: Ben Linders
insights.so_what: A segmentation model for where AI tooling will and will not pay off, usable to qualify which enterprise buyers convert AI spend into delivery outcomes.
insights.locator: they identified seven unique team profiles in the data

insights.claim: The 'constrained by process' profile shows high burnout, high friction, low individual effectiveness and low time spent on valuable work, yet has the best software delivery stability of any profile with only slightly lower throughput - stability bought at the cost of the people.
insights.speaker: Ben Linders
insights.so_what: Demonstrates that good delivery metrics can mask an unsustainable organization - a caution against reading DORA-style dashboards as a proxy for organizational health.
insights.locator: For this team profile, burnout is high

themes.theme: Seven Capabilities That Convert AI Adoption into Outcomes

insights.claim: DORA identified seven capabilities that, combined with AI adoption, drive better outcomes: a clear and communicated AI stance, healthy data ecosystems, AI-accessible internal data, strong version control practices, working in small batches, user-centric focus, and quality internal platforms.
insights.speaker: Ben Linders
insights.so_what: Three of the seven are data and platform infrastructure, which locates the enterprise AI bottleneck in data plumbing rather than in models.
insights.locator: They identified seven capabilities that, when combined with AI adoption

insights.claim: AI puts direct pressure on the long-established finding that small batches improve delivery performance, because models suggest large change sets and pull requests that are harder to review, harder to assess for fitness, and carry more risk.
insights.speaker: Ben Linders
insights.so_what: Explains the instability finding mechanically and creates a product opening for tooling that decomposes AI output into independently deployable units.
insights.locator: AI puts pressure on this idea because the models can suggest

insights.claim: The recommended mitigation is for teams to collaborate with their AI assistants to break large changes down into smaller, independently deployable units rather than accepting model-sized change sets.
insights.speaker: Ben Linders
insights.so_what: A concrete practice change that AI coding vendors could productize as a default behaviour - a differentiator once instability becomes a visible enterprise cost.
insights.locator: Teams can use these insights to collaborate

themes.theme: Internal Platforms as the AI Distribution Layer

insights.claim: Quality internal platforms are the optimal mechanism for making models, workflows and other AI capabilities accessible across an entire organization, which is what drives adoption and value realization.
insights.speaker: Ben Linders
insights.so_what: Positions internal developer platforms as the enterprise distribution channel for AI capability - a strategic control point for platform-engineering vendors.
insights.locator: What role can platforms play in AI adoption

insights.claim: Platforms go beyond access by shifting complexity downward and hiding it from users, so that a mandated security policy can be enforced automatically for any new solution, improving compliance while abstracting the policy away from developers.
insights.speaker: Ben Linders
insights.so_what: Compliance-by-platform is the argument that gets AI governance funded in regulated industries - watch for policy enforcement moving into platform layers.
insights.locator: Platforms also allow organizations to shift complexity down

insights.claim: AI's real contribution is unlocking optionality - teams can prototype five things in less time than one previously took - which matters because organizations are bad at knowing what users want, so the right response is building many things, trying them, and debating them as a team.
insights.speaker: Ben Linders
insights.so_what: Reframes AI value as cheaper experimentation rather than cheaper labour, which favours products that support parallel prototyping and rapid discard.
insights.locator: AI can do things a lot faster; it unlocks optionality

insights.claim: Harvey's prescription for applying the research is to assess current state, set priorities and develop a culture of continuous improvement, treating DORA findings as hypotheses to contextualize rather than prescriptions to copy.
insights.speaker: Ben Linders
insights.so_what: Signals that benchmark data is being positioned as diagnostic input, not standard - limiting the case for one-size-fits-all AI mandates.
insights.quote: Take the findings and use them as your hypothesis
insights.locator: For putting research into practice, Harvey suggested
